title: Builder Signals · 2026-09-29
summary: Follow Builders 今日捕捉到 25 条 X 动态、1 集播客、0 篇博客；本站精选 12 条高信号内容。

featured.title: Thibault Sottiaux · OpenAI Codex & ChatGPT 负责人
featured.summaryEn: OpenAI's Codex and ChatGPT lead Thibault Sottiaux argues that code freeze before releases isn't really a thing anymore, and that in the future code might even be generated online per request according to some constraints. The implication: when code generation approaches zero marginal cost and can be done by agents in seconds, the traditional governance model built around "lock the repo, run regression, ship in a window" loses its foundation. For enterprise IT, change management, audit trails, and compliance tracea…
featured.insightZh: OpenAI Codex 与 ChatGPT 负责人 Thibault Sottiaux 抛了一个关于软件发布流程的判断：发版前的"代码冻结"（code freeze）已经基本不再是一件事了，而未来代码甚至可能是按请求在线生成的——根据某些约束条件实时产出。这句话背后的含义是：当代码生成的边际成本趋近于零、且可由 agent 在秒级完成时，传统那套"锁定代码库—回归测试—发布窗口"的工程治理范式会失去存在基础。对于大型企业 IT 而言，这意味着变更管理、审计留痕、合规回溯这些围绕"代码是静态资产"建立的流程，未来需要重新设计。

featured.title: Peter Yang · Roblox 产品负责人、AI 教程创作者
featured.summaryEn: Peter Yang notes that almost nobody has fond memories of the SaaS or business software they used back in the day, but everyone remembers their favorite games — games are the software with the longest staying power in our memories. He jokes that LLM models are probably the inverse of that. The underlying point is a product one: models are commoditizing fast, and emotional attachment won't accrue to the model itself — only to the experience layer wrapped around it.
featured.insightZh: Peter Yang 提了一个关于软件"记忆留存度"的观察：几乎没有人会深情回忆当年用过的 SaaS 或企业软件，但每个人都记得自己最爱的游戏。游戏才是在我们记忆中存活最久的软件品类。他半开玩笑地补了一句：LLM 模型大概是这个规律的反面——用得最频繁、但最没有人会怀念某个具体版本。这个对比其实点出了一个产品层面的现实：模型本身正在快速商品化，情感依附和记忆点不会发生在模型身上，而只会发生在包裹模型的那层体验上。

featured.title: Box's Aaron Levie: On Reinventing Yourself in the AI Age and Enterprise Diffusion
featured.summaryEn: There is a vast gap between model capability and enterprise workflow, and bridging it is a multi-trillion-dollar application-layer opportunity; AI diffusion beyond coding will be far slower than Silicon Valley expects — and that slowness is precisely where the application layer's value comes from. Aaron Levie makes the most systematic bull case for the application layer heard recently. The "model wrapper" thesis is working because people underestimated how long and deep the bridge from model capability to real enterprise workflow actually is. Even a perfect superintelligence still has to connect to other data systems, handle human-in-the-loop moments, sit idle through process delays, absorb business-process change management, and deal with unmodernized legacy systems. Those are operational chores that a research org least wants to attack. His historical analogy: ten years ago, looking a…
featured.insightZh: 模型和工作流之间存在巨大的鸿沟，跨越这道鸿沟的"应用层"价值以万亿美元计；而 AI 在编码之外的扩散会比硅谷预期的慢得多，慢的原因恰恰就是应用层价值的来源。 Box CEO Aaron Levie 在这期 Sequoia 的 Training Data 里给出了近期最系统的一次"应用层多头"论证。他的核心判断是：过去两年被嘲笑的"模型套壳"其实走通了，因为人们低估了一件事——在真实企业里，你需要一座桥把模型能力连到企业实际的工作流上，而这座桥非常长、非常深。模型可能是世界上最聪明的超级智能，但工作流仍然要求它连接其他数据系统、仍然有人在环的交互节点、仍然有流程延迟导致 agent 空转、仍然有业务流程的变革管理、仍然有没现代化的遗留系统。这五到十件事都是操作层面的脏活，而一个典型的研究型组织最不想干的就是逐个攻克它们。他拿历史做类比：十年前看着 AWS 和 GCP 在数据领域的动作，你绝不会预测出 Snowflake 和 Databricks 的存在——你会觉得"基础设施本身不就干了这事吗"。智能这一层会重演同样的剧本。 关于模型选型与开源权重，Levie 提供了难得的一手数据。Box 有两套 eval：一套公开的 complex work eval（覆盖生命科学、金融服务、公共部门、科技等领域的文档密集型任务），一套是用 Box 自己实例和员工真实用法构成的保留集。他的观察是各家模型表现与编码能力高度相关，唯一显著例外是 Gemini——在部分用例上明显好于其编码表现所预示的水平，他猜测跟 Gemini 生态所需的工具使用能力有关。目前 Grog、Muse、Fable 类和 GPT-5.6 系列基本是贴身缠斗。开源权重模型的采用率"比大众想象的高、比企业实际想要的低、比五年后的水平低得多得多"，且他估计其中 30% 以上的动机纯粹是"想试试新东西"而非成本。他引用 Decagon 的 Jesse 的观点作为长期框架：闭源能力继续指数级上升，但每个成熟下来的用例都可以剥离到开源权重上去——于是你会看到 Anthropic/OpenAI 收入爆表和开源权重指数增长同时发…

items.title: Thariq · Anthropic Claude Code 团队
items.summaryEn: Thariq from Anthropic's Claude Code team voices a rarely discussed worry: he is most afraid of us eating the productivity gains of agents by just becoming lazier. This is an organizational risk, not a technical one — when execution cost drops, net output stays flat unless ambition and quality bars rise in step. For any enterprise modeling AI transformation ROI, this belongs in the assumptions: whether efficiency gains materialize depends entirely on where the saved time goes.
items.insightZh: Claude Code 团队的 Thariq 说出了一个很少被公开讨论的担忧：他最害怕的，是我们把 agent 带来的生产力增益，通过"人变得更懒"这件事全部吃掉。这不是技术风险而是组织风险——当执行成本下降时，如果不同步提高目标的野心度和质量标准，净产出可能完全不变，只是人类投入的注意力变少了。对任何正在做 AI 转型 ROI 测算的企业来说，这是个值得写进假设条件里的变量：效率工具的收益能不能兑现，取决于节省下来的时间被投到了哪里。

items.title: Guillermo Rauch · Vercel CEO
items.summaryEn: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch ported his Mini web browser from Electron + Bun to Rust & Swift — faster, more secure, and shockingly nicer to iterate on. The architecture is the interesting part: the `cef` crate bundles up-to-date Chromium for Safari-like UX; `fx acp` embeds an agent without bloating the app, talking to his local fx CLI over ACP, which in turn manages the browser via an MCP server. Ditching Electron got him Liquid Glass, faster boots, a more Mac-native feel, and fine-grained focus/input control that i…
items.insightZh: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 把自己的 Mini 浏览器从 Electron + Bun 移植到了 Rust + Swift，结论很明确：更快、更安全，而且迭代体验反而比 Electron 更好。技术细节值得关注——他用 `cef` crate 打包最新版 Chromium，拿到了接近 Safari 的原生 UX；用 `fx acp` 在不撑大应用体积的前提下嵌入 agent，agent 通过 ACP 协议与本地 fx CLI 通信，fx 再通过 MCP server 反过来控制浏览器。放弃 Electron 让他拿到了 Liquid Glass、更快的启动、更 Mac 原生的手感，以及那些在 JS 里堪称噩梦的细粒度焦点与输入控制。他的大判断是：原生是未来，桌面和云端都是——整个软件世界"原生化"的速度会比大多数人预期的快得多，正如 DHH 在 Rails World 上暗示的那样。Vercel 押注的 Fluid 正是为支撑这一趋势（无论你选 Rust、Go 还是 Zig）。顺带一提，这整个项目是用 Opus 5.5 和 Sol 6 构建的。

items.title: Aaron Levie · Box CEO
items.summaryEn: Box CEO Aaron Levie draws a split worth taking seriously at the strategy level. Some parts of the economy benefit from the friction customers face when changing habits — there, switching costs collapse and competition intensifies dramatically until a new equilibrium forms between disruptors and incumbents. Other markets are hurt by friction — healthcare, travel, local services, certain information services — and agents will unlock economic activity that was previously too frictionful to happen, making them net ben…
items.insightZh: Box CEO Aaron Levie 给出了一个值得企业战略层认真对待的二分：当 agent 开始替用户做出最优或最高效的选择时，经济体中会出现两类截然相反的结果。一类市场原本就是靠"用户换东西很麻烦"这层摩擦在赚钱的——在这些市场里，转换成本会急剧下降，竞争会剧烈加剧，直到颠覆者和在位者之间达成新的均衡。另一类市场则是被摩擦所伤害的——医疗、旅行、本地服务、某些信息服务——在这些地方，agent 会把原本因为太麻烦而没发生的交易释放出来，做大整个盘子，因此是净受益方。他的结论是：一个被"不知疲倦地为我们的目标工作的 agent"深度中介化的未来，不可能跟今天以同样的方式运转。

items.title: Garry Tan · Y Combinator 总裁兼 CEO
items.summaryEn: YC President Garry Tan spent two days taking shots at anti-bot defenses, and the technical read underneath is real: "Oh I can do this with CDP" means you have not actually hit any real anti-bot yet. That's a warning for every team building agentic browsing, automated procurement, or AI assistants that act on a user's behalf — the gap between a working demo and durable automation on live commercial sites is a full stack of fingerprinting, behavioral analysis, and escalating countermeasures. Tan sits firmly on the o…
items.insightZh: YC 总裁 Garry Tan 这两天连着对"反爬虫/反自动化"开火，观点带刺但指向一个真实的技术现实：如果你觉得"用 CDP（Chrome DevTools Protocol）就能搞定"，那说明你还没撞上过真正的反机器人防护。这对当下所有做 agentic browsing、自动化采购、AI 助手代操作的团队都是一记提醒——demo 环境下能跑通的浏览器自动化，和在真实的商业网站上长期稳定运行，中间隔着一整套指纹识别、行为分析和对抗升级。他本人的立场是站在开放一侧的（"反爬是 loser 行为"），但这恰恰说明这场攻防会成为 agent 商业化路上的长期摩擦点。

items.title: Matt Turck · FirstMark Capital 投资人、MAD Podcast 主播
items.summaryEn: Matt Turck of FirstMark Capital flags a persistent and ironic pattern: AI researchers who understand how AI actually works tend to believe in neither AI doom nor massive uncontrollable acceleration, while non-researchers with limited knowledge hold very definite and certain views. Useful heuristic for decision-makers evaluating AI risk narratives: confidence strength and information quality are often inversely correlated.
items.insightZh: FirstMark 的 Matt Turck 指出了一个持续存在且颇具讽刺意味的分布规律：越是真正理解 AI 如何运作的研究者，越倾向于既不相信 AI 末日论、也不相信不可控的大爆发；而那些对技术细节了解有限的非研究者，反而在这个话题上持有极其明确、极其笃定的观点。这个观察对企业决策者有直接用处——当你在评估 AI 风险叙事时，信心的强度和信息的质量往往是负相关的。

items.title: Zara Zhang · 独立创作者、Follow Builders 主理人
items.summaryEn: Zara Zhang shared two reflections this week. On being asked why she posts without monetizing: self-expression is an innate human instinct requiring no utilitarian justification, and influence is far more valuable than money. The second is the one worth circulating internally — new technology can be so dazzling and flashy that it blinds us to the ways in which it's not working, and sometimes makes you feel that if something isn't working it's probably your fault rather than the technology's, because the world is mo…
items.insightZh: Zara Zhang 这周发了两条内容策略与技术认知上的思考。第一条回应"为什么一直发内容却不变现"的质疑，她给出两点：自我表达是人类的本能，不需要任何功利性理由来证成；而影响力本身远比金钱有价值。第二条更值得企业内部传阅——新技术可能炫目到让我们对"它其实没跑通"的那些地方视而不见；更糟的是，它会让你觉得如果某件事没跑通，那大概是你自己的问题而不是技术的问题，因为世界在飞速前进，每个人看起来都比你领先。这恰好是当下大量 AI 落地项目中"不敢说出口的真相"的心理机制。

items.title: Nikunj Kothari · FPV Ventures 合伙人
items.summaryEn: FPV Ventures partner Nikunj Kothari's hands-on read on Astra: it's absurd. His usage pattern is the signal — give it decently hard *verifiable* end-to-end tasks with the right tools, and watch it fly. The "verifiable end-to-end" qualifier is the key constraint: this generation of agents is bounded less by raw task difficulty than by whether a task has a clear success criterion and a closed tool loop. Direct implication for enterprise pilot selection: start with processes that already have explicit acceptance crite…
items.insightZh: FPV Ventures 合伙人 Nikunj Kothari 对 Astra 的实测反馈很直接：这东西离谱（absurd）。他的用法值得注意——给它有一定难度、且结果可被验证（verifiable）的端到端任务，配上合适的工具，然后看着它跑完。"可验证的端到端任务"这个限定条件是关键：当前一代 agent 的能力边界，很大程度上不取决于任务难度本身，而取决于任务是否具备清晰的成功判据和可调用的工具闭环。这对企业选型有直接指导意义——先找那些有明确验收标准的流程下手。

items.title: Peter Steinberger · OpenClaw 核心开发者
items.summaryEn: OpenClaw's Peter Steinberger, discussing how to distribute CI load beyond a single sponsor, outlined a concrete plan: let codex decide which tests actually need to run, drastically nix CI, and run the full suite hourly instead. This is an early instance of agents participating in engineering *governance* decisions — not writing code, but handling test-selection scheduling that has historically been solved with heuristics or brute-force full runs. If it holds up, both CI cost structure and feedback latency get rede…
items.insightZh: OpenClaw 的 Peter Steinberger 在讨论 CI 成本分摊时抛出了一个具体的工程计划：让 codex 自己决定哪些测试真正需要跑，从而大幅削减 CI，改为每小时跑一次完整测试。这是"agent 参与工程治理决策"的一个早期实例——不是让 AI 写代码，而是让 AI 来做"测试选择"这类原本靠启发式规则或全量兜底解决的调度问题。如果这套做法被验证有效，CI 成本结构和反馈速度都会被重新定义。

items.title: Dan Shipper · Every CEO
items.summaryEn: Every CEO Dan Shipper's one-liner on the state of advertising and consumer industries: an industry built on modeling humans as rational agents panics as humans adopt rational agents. Behind the quip is a serious issue — when purchase decisions are executed by agents, the space for brand premium, impulse buying, and channel friction that traditional marketing depends on gets compressed hard. It's the same coin as Aaron Levie's point today about collapsing switching costs.
items.insightZh: Every 的 CEO Dan Shipper 用一句话概括了当下广告与消费行业的处境：一个建立在"把人类建模为理性 agent"这个假设之上的行业，正在因为人类真的开始使用理性 agent 而陷入恐慌。这句俏皮话背后是个严肃议题——当购买决策由 agent 代为执行时，品牌溢价、冲动消费、渠道摩擦这些传统营销赖以生存的非理性行为空间会被大幅压缩。这与 Aaron Levie 今天关于"转换成本崩塌"的判断是同一枚硬币的两面。
